request.spec:
Show a rate calendar: for each grade and each month of the sheet's today's calendar year, the
rate in force on the first day of that month (n/a when none).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show a rate calendar: for each grade and each month of the sheet's today's calendar year, the
rate in force on the first day of that month (n/a when none).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rate calendar is in, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**The calendar.** A new section, `src/main/frontend/features/rates/calendar.slot.tsx`, shows a table with one row per grade and one column per month of the sheet's today's year. Each cell (`rate-month-<grade>-<YYYY-MM>`) shows the rate in force on the 1st of that month, or `n/a` when there is none. It works the rate out the same way "in force today" does (`rateOn`), so end dates and rates inherited from parent sheets are handled. No server change was needed for this part.

**A second fix, outside the request.** The first three tests passed straight away, but scenario 3 failed in the pools/crews checks. That scenario transfers Cam, who leads crew C1, to another sheet. It then expects C1 to still exist with no lead, and its one remaining member Ada at a 100.00 share. The app deleted any crew whose lead was transferred, and its code comments said that was intended. I followed the test and changed that rule:
- **New migration:** `V82__crew_lead_optional.sql` lets a crew have no lead.
- **Transfer:** `ApplyTransfer` now keeps the crews the person leads, with their members and no lead, instead of deleting them.
- **Crew as a pool:** `RespondWithPools` splits the shares among the members only when there's no lead. A crew with no lead and no members shows as an empty pool rather than crashing.
- **Sheet clone:** `ApplyClone` copies a crew with no lead as it is; before, it would have crashed on one.

Creating a crew still requires a lead. If deleting the crew on transfer was the intended rule, scenario 3 can't pass without changing the test, so this needs your decision.
